preamble: Fronting of the uvular ejective [qʼ] to the velar ejective [kʼ], keeping glottalization. In most Mayan branches (Huastecan, Yucatecan, Cholan-Tseltalan and others), Proto-Mayan *qʼ merged with *kʼ together with the parallel merger of plain *q with *k, while Kʼicheʼan and Mamean keep the uvulars. In Laz (Kartvelian), *qʼ became kʼ after another ejective in a cluster (tʼqʼ > tʼkʼ, tsʼqʼ > tsʼkʼ) in Vitse-Arkabi, Khopa-Arkabi and Chkhala, whereas Atina, Vizha and Artasheni drop it there.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Mayan to Huastecan, Yucatecan and Cholan-Tseltalan

examples.note: All branches except Kʼicheʼan–Mamean and some Qʼanjobʼalan merged *qʼ with kʼ (England 1994), parallel to *q > k; Kʼicheʼ and Mam keep /qʼ/.
Meaning shifted to 'blackberry shrub, thorns' (Vitse-Arkabi), 'grass, weed' (Chkhala). Atina/Vizha/Artasheni მტა mta; Megrelian ტყა tʼqʼa and Georgian ტყე tʼqʼe 'forest'.

examples.to: Laz მწკოლი mtsʼkʼoli, მწკო mtsʼkʼo (Khopa, Arkabi, Vitse)
examples.note: Georgian წ is [tsʼ]; Laz Latin mǯǩo. Atina/Vizha/Artasheni მწუ mtsʼu; Georgian წყავი.
